findings.title: AppendTurnAsync uses enum strings that do not satisfy entry table CHECK constraints
findings.evidence: `InputModality = turn.InputModality.ToString(),` and `TurnType = turn.TurnType.ToString(),` while the table requires `CHECK (input_modality IN ('voice', 'text'))` and `CHECK (turn_type IN ('execution', 'clarification', 'confirmation', 'ambiguity_resolution'))`.
findings.problem: The write path serializes `InputModality` and `TurnType` as PascalCase enum names, but the schema only accepts lowercase/snake_case literals.
findings.why_it_matters: Core entry inserts will fail as written, or require undocumented remapping that would also affect hash reproducibility.
findings.proposed_fix: Define one explicit persisted-string mapping for each enum and use it for both hashing and SQL inserts; add tests for every enum value.

findings.title: WriteDecorationAsync cannot insert any documented decoration type with the shown enum conversion
findings.evidence: `Type = type.ToString().ToLowerInvariant()` but the schema requires `decoration_type IN ('rationale_extraction','manual_annotation','ambiguity_context','integrity_event')`.
findings.problem: Lowercasing a C# enum name cannot produce the required snake_case literals shown in the CHECK constraint.
findings.why_it_matters: `DecorationWriterTests` are listed as build-breaking in Section 13, so this path fails required tests and any runtime decoration insert.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a stable enum-to-storage mapping for `DecorationType` and reuse it in inserts, reads, and hashing/tests.

findings.title: DbUp journal placement creates a bootstrap dependency on a schema that does not exist yet
findings.evidence: The spec says migrations are "Idempotent via DbUp's journal table (`dhf.schema_versions`)" while `001_initial_schema.sql` itself contains `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS dhf;` and `CREATE TABLE dhf.schema_versions (...)`.
findings.problem: DbUp must access its journal table before it can determine which scripts to run, but the journal table is defined inside the schema created by the first migration.
findings.why_it_matters: Fresh-database startup can fail or require undocumented bootstrap code outside this spec.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify a bootstrap step that creates the `dhf` schema and journal table before migration discovery, or move the journal table to a pre-existing schema.

findings.title: OpenOrResumeSessionAsync does not actually serialize decisions per workstation
findings.evidence: The comment says "Advisory lock to serialize open-or-resume decisions per workstation" but the key is `var lockKey = $"dhf_session_open:{metadata.WorkstationId}:{addinSessionId}";`.
findings.problem: Different `addinSessionId` values on the same workstation take different advisory locks, so concurrent new-load events on one workstation are not serialized.
findings.why_it_matters: This can violate the documented split/resume lifecycle by allowing overlapping close/open decisions on the same workstation.
findings.proposed_fix: Lock on workstation only for open/resume, or add a DB constraint guaranteeing at most one open session per workstation and document the retry behavior.

findings.title: The spec promises retry-on-race behavior for session open, but the shown method has no retry logic
findings.evidence: The note says "the second will fail on unique-violation and retry via the lookup path," but `OpenOrResumeSessionAsync` contains no catch/retry loop for `INSERT` or transaction commit failures.
findings.problem: The documented fallback path is not implementable from the provided method contract/code because SQLSTATE `23505`/`40001` are never retried.
findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent orchestrator startup will surface transient failures instead of deterministically resuming or opening a session.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify bounded retries for unique-violation and serialization-failure, with re-read of the open session inside each retry attempt.

findings.title: AppendTurnAsync allows entries to be written into a closed session
findings.evidence: `AppendTurnAsync` reads/inserts by `session_id` only; Section 6.2 says shutdown closes sessions by setting `ended_at = NOW()`, but no append-path check references `ended_at`.
findings.problem: A stale caller can continue appending to a session after it has been closed.
findings.why_it_matters: This breaks the spec's epoch/session-boundary guarantees and makes `ended_at` non-authoritative.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate `ended_at IS NULL` inside the append transaction or add a DB trigger/constraint rejecting entry inserts into closed sessions.

findings.title: Tool-call addin session IDs are not enforced to match the owning DHF session
findings.evidence: `ToolCallRecord` contains `public required string AddinSessionId { get; init; }`, `dhf.sessions` stores `addin_session_id`, and `AppendTurnAsync` inserts mapped tool calls without comparing them to the session row.
findings.problem: The API permits mixed-epoch tool calls inside one entry and the schema has no constraint preventing it.
findings.why_it_matters: This undermines SDR-04-004/005 because the ledger can record child rows from a different add-in epoch than the parent session.
findings.proposed_fix: Either remove redundant per-tool-call `addin_session_id` or enforce equality with the owning session's `addin_session_id` during append and at the DB layer.

findings.title: Speculative: hashed timestamp normalization is unspecified across .NET and Postgres storage
findings.evidence: `Timestamp` is hashed before insert in `AppendTurnAsync`, and validation later "Recomputes `record_hash` ... from stored column values," but Section 4.1 defines no `DateTimeOffset`/`TIMESTAMPTZ` normalization or precision rule.
findings.problem: Speculative: `TIMESTAMPTZ` can normalize offset/precision relative to the in-memory `DateTimeOffset`, so the value hashed at write time may not serialize identically when read back for validation.
findings.why_it_matters: False integrity failures become likely for non-UTC or sub-microsecond timestamps, making shallow/deep validation unreliable.
findings.proposed_fix: Require UTC normalization and fixed precision before hashing and before INSERT, or store the canonical timestamp string that was hashed.

findings.title: The read API exposes undefined DTO contracts to downstream consumers
findings.evidence: `IDhfRepository` returns `DhfSessionSummary`, `DhfSessionDetail`, `DhfEntrySummary`, `DhfEntryDetail`, `ToolCallRow`, and `DecorationRow`, but none of these types are defined in this spec or listed as imported dependencies.
findings.problem: Consumers cannot implement or test against a stable repository contract because the shapes, nullability, and ordering semantics are missing.
findings.why_it_matters: This will create integration churn with SPEC-06 and makes `DhfRepositoryTests` underspecified.
findings.proposed_fix: Define all repository DTOs and method contracts, including field lists, nullability, sort order, and pagination semantics.

findings.title: Repeated validation failures can append unbounded duplicate integrity_event decorations
findings.evidence: Section 8.2 says "Any integrity check failure ... is written as an `integrity_event` decoration" and Section 10.1 says shallow validation "runs on every viewer page load."
findings.problem: The same persistent mismatch can generate a new decoration on every page load because no deduplication or idempotency rule is defined.
findings.why_it_matters: This creates storage growth, noisy duplicates, and turns a nominally read-triggered validation path into an unbounded write source.
findings.proposed_fix: Define deduplication rules for `integrity_event` rows or forbid validator-triggered writes during viewer page loads.

findings.title: The regulatory mapping claims per-entry user identity, but the schema stores identity only per session
findings.evidence: Section 12 states `User identity stored per entry`, but `user_identity` exists on `dhf.sessions` only; `dhf.entries` has no user identity column.
findings.problem: The document claims a granularity of attribution that the data model does not implement.
findings.why_it_matters: This misstates audit capability and hides the fact that a user change within a session cannot be reconstructed per entry.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the claim to `per session` or add immutable user identity fields to `dhf.entries` if per-entry attribution is required.

findings.title: The decoration mutability policy is internally contradictory
findings.evidence: SDR-04-002 says `dhf.entry_decorations` is `insert-only` and `never mutated in place`, but 005 says `UPDATE and DELETE are permitted for operational cleanup, so no trigger.`
findings.problem: The spec gives two incompatible rules for whether decoration rows may be modified or deleted.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementers and tests cannot tell whether decoration mutation is a defect or an allowed maintenance operation.
findings.proposed_fix: Choose one policy and encode it consistently in schema, code, and tests; if cleanup is allowed, document the exact allowed operations and audit trail requirements.

top_3_must_fix: Define one canonical enum-to-storage mapping for all persisted literals; the current `ToString()`/`ToLowerInvariant()` paths do not satisfy the schema and will fail inserts.
Fix session lifecycle concurrency semantics by aligning the lock scope with workstation-level serialization, adding the promised retry logic, and rejecting appends to closed sessions.
Specify hash-stable persistence rules for timestamp normalization/precision and bootstrap the DbUp journal/schema so a fresh database can actually start.
